extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines the coverage and billing requirements for home health services in accordance

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: with CMS regulations. Medicare-certified home health agencies (HHA) may provide these services to

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: eligible members who meet the specific criteria for home health care. 1 Currently, the plan allows up

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: to 8 visits without prior authorization. Beginning January 1, 2026, the plan will allow up to 5 visits

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: without prior authorization. Any visits beyond the allowed threshold require clinical review

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: and authorization. Notices of Admission (NOAs) are not required to initiate treatment.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: House calls and unskilled home care are not considered home health services and are excluded from

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: coverage under the home health benefit. 1

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Home Health Agency (HHA) : A Medicare-certified provider of home health services.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Home Health Services : A range of healthcare services provided in the beneficiary's home for illness

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: or injury.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Intermittent Skilled Nursing Care : Nursing care provided fewer than seven days per week or less

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: than 8 hours per day over a 21-day (or shorter) period.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Negative Pressure-Wound Therapy (NPWT) : Application of negative pressure across a wound.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Notice of Admission (NOA) : One-time submission to establish that the beneficiary is under a home

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: health period of care and trigger home health consolidated billing edits.

extracted_content.title: Eligibility Criteria
extracted_content.content: Eligibility Criteria

extracted_content.title: Eligibility Criteria
extracted_content.content: CMS requires certain conditions to be met for home health services to be covered. These criteria

extracted_content.title: Eligibility Criteria
extracted_content.content: ensure that the care is medically necessary and provided according to federal guidelines. 1

extracted_content.title: Eligibility Criteria
extracted_content.content: ● Homebound Status : The member must be considered homebound, meaning they face

extracted_content.title: Eligibility Criteria
extracted_content.content: significant difficulty leaving their residence due to their medical condition or injury.

extracted_content.title: Eligibility Criteria
extracted_content.content: ● Physician Certification : The ordering physician must certify the member's homebound status,

extracted_content.title: Eligibility Criteria
extracted_content.content: establish a plan of care, review it periodically, and review and sign the re-certification at least

extracted_content.title: Eligibility Criteria
extracted_content.content: every 60 days.

extracted_content.title: Eligibility Criteria
extracted_content.content: ● Plan of Care : Providers must follow a detailed plan created by the physician or allowed

extracted_content.title: Eligibility Criteria
extracted_content.content: practitioner, specifying the required services and their frequency.

extracted_content.title: Eligibility Criteria
extracted_content.content: ● Require Skilled Nursing or Therapy Services : Services provider must require the specialized

extracted_content.title: Eligibility Criteria
extracted_content.content: skills of a licensed clinician, such as a nurse or therapist.

extracted_content.title: Eligibility Criteria
extracted_content.content: ● Face-to-Face Encounter : Provider must ensure the member has had a face-to-face consultation

extracted_content.title: Eligibility Criteria
extracted_content.content: with a physician or an approved non-physician practitioner (NPP), such as nurse or physician

extracted_content.title: Eligibility Criteria
extracted_content.content: assistant, within 90 days prior to or 30 days following the start of care and 60 days thereafter

extracted_content.title: Eligibility Criteria
extracted_content.content: for re-certification.

extracted_content.title: Eligibility Criteria
extracted_content.content: Claims billing for services not covered under home health care or that fail to meet established

extracted_content.title: Eligibility Criteria
extracted_content.content: eligibility criteria will be denied.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: Devoted Health processes claims following CMS guidelines, with the exception of prior authorizations

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: and Notices of Admission (NOAs). Payments are made based on the Patient-Driven Grouping Model

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: (PDGM), and providers must adhere to all relevant documentation requirements. Compliance with

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: these guidelines is essential to prevent claim delays or denials.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: Patient-Driven Grouping Model (PDGM)

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: Unless otherwise specified in your contract, Devoted Health follows CMS's PDGM for payment,

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: focusing on clinical characteristics rather than volume. Low-Utilization Payment Adjustment (LUPA)

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: rates apply if the number of visits for a particular member falls below a specific threshold. Providers

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: must be aware of the threshold for each case to ensure accurate billing. Reimbursement includes

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: routine and non-routine supplies and services; however, the following are to be billed separately:

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: injectable osteoporosis drugs, durable medical equipment (DME), and disposable device-assisted

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT). 3

extracted_content.title: Documentation Requirements
extracted_content.content: Documentation Requirements

extracted_content.title: Documentation Requirements
extracted_content.content: Providers must adhere to CMS documentation requirements for home health services, including

extracted_content.title: Documentation Requirements
extracted_content.content: signed orders, detailed records of the member's condition, the face-to-face encounter record, plan of

extracted_content.title: Documentation Requirements
extracted_content.content: care, and ongoing assessments. Once established, regular updates to the plan of care and periodic

extracted_content.title: Documentation Requirements
extracted_content.content: physician reviews are required every 60 days. Failure to meet these documentation and review

extracted_content.title: Documentation Requirements
extracted_content.content: requirements may result in claim denials.

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements
extracted_content.content: Claim Submission Requirements

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements
extracted_content.content: Providers must follow these CMS guidelines for accurate and timely claim submission. 3

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements
extracted_content.content: ● 30-Day Episode : Each episode of care should be submitted as a single claim with a 30-day

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements
extracted_content.content: cycle. Claims should be accurate and reflect all services provided within the 30-day episode.

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements
extracted_content.content: ● Billing Visits : Each visit should be billed by date of service, with the correct revenue and

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements
extracted_content.content: CPT/HCPCS codes associated with the service rendered on that day.

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements
extracted_content.content: ○ Revenue Codes : Providers must include a valid HIPPS code and bill it with the 0023

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements
extracted_content.content: revenue code to ensure accurate pricing. Claims missing a HIPPS code or submitted

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements
extracted_content.content: without the 0023 revenue code may be denied or delayed in processing.

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements
extracted_content.content: ● Claim Format : Providers should submit claims via the 837i (CMS-1450/UB-04) for claims. If

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements
extracted_content.content: certified as an DME supplier, providers may use the 837P (CMS 1500) for claims related to DME.
